sources.entry: DPDK Programmer's Guide - Defines the full bypass model, pinned poll-mode cores with no interrupts, that every kernel path is measured against.

summary.title: Programmer's Guide
summary.one_liner: This DPDK programmer's guide index shows the table of contents of the library documentation, covering memory, CPU, packet processing, device and utility libraries.
takeaways: DPDK's documentation is organized into foundation principles, memory management, CPU management, packet processing, device, protocol, high-level and utility library sections.
Packet processing libraries include hash, membership, IP fragmentation and reassembly, GRO/GSO, ACL, LPM/LPM6, RIB and FIB.
Device libraries cover Ethernet, bonding, vhost, cryptography, security, compression, regex, DMA, GPU, event and raw devices.
Utility libraries include ring, stack, timer, RCU, log, metrics, telemetry, and packet capture (pcap and BPF).
summary.summary: This page is the table of contents for the DPDK Programmer's Guide, not the full text of any single chapter. It lists the guide's sections: foundation principles, memory and CPU management, and numbered chapters for packet processing, device, protocol, high-level and utility libraries. The listing itself gives no implementation details, so use it as a map to the individual library chapters. The listing's note frames DPDK as the full kernel-bypass model, with pinned poll-mode cores and no interrupts.
